prompt:
Fix simultaneous renaming of a virtual asset registry. This is an in-memory mapping, not filesystem operations.
validation.rename_map(registry, changes) returns a new source-to-target dict.
registry must be a dict whose keys are nonempty strings (case/whitespace significant); values may contain nested data.
changes must be a list of dicts with required source and target nonempty string fields; extra fields are ignored.
Every source must exist in the original registry. Sources and targets must each be unique across all changes.
A target already in the original registry is allowed only if that key is also a source in this batch.
Self-renames, chains, and swaps/cycles are valid. Validate the entire input, including registry keys when changes is empty.
All invalid inputs raise ValueError. Do not mutate any input on success or failure.
operations.apply_renames(registry, changes) validates using rename_map and returns a new dict, iterating ORIGINAL registry order,
substituting each renamed key and retaining unchanged keys. Values must be deep copies, independent of the inputs and of
other returned entries even if original values shared references. Empty registry and empty changes are valid.
Only edit renames/validation.py, renames/operations.py. Run the documented public test command after the final edits.

def rename_map(registry, changes):
    return {item['source']: item['target'] for item in changes}

prompt:
Fix a small byte-serving helper. Implement the following deliberately limited single-range contract (no network calls).
ranges.parse_range(header, size) returns inclusive (start, end). size must be an int (not bool), >= 0.
header must exactly match bytes=N-M, bytes=N-, or bytes=-N, using one or more ASCII digits per number;
leading zeroes are allowed. No whitespace, signs, additional ranges, or trailing characters are allowed.
For N-M require M >= N, N < size, and clamp M to size-1. For N- return (N, size-1), requiring N < size.
For -N require N > 0 and return the last min(N, size) bytes. Any supplied range with size 0 is invalid.
All invalid inputs raise ValueError.
response.serve(data, header=None) requires bytes data, raises ValueError otherwise, and returns exactly a dict
with status, body, content_range. With no header return status 200, the entire data, content_range None (also for empty data).
With a header use parse_range and return status 206, the inclusive slice, and content_range 'bytes START-END/TOTAL'.
Even a range covering all data returns 206. Do not alter inputs.
Only edit windows/ranges.py, windows/response.py. Run the documented public test command after the final edits.

prompt:
Repair deterministic replay of an in-memory event stream.
validation.normalize(event) accepts a dict with required id/key (nonempty strings, exact/case-sensitive),
version (int >=1, not bool), and action ('put' or 'delete'). A put must contain value (any nested data, including None);
a delete must NOT contain value. Extra fields are ignored. Return a new dict with exactly these recognized fields,
deep-copying value. Invalid input raises ValueError.
replay.replay(events) requires a list and returns {'values': dict, 'versions': dict}, starting from empty state.
Validate every event with normalize. An already-seen id with the same normalized content is an idempotent duplicate:
ignore it, even after later versions. Reusing an id with different normalized content raises ValueError.
Every new id must have a version strictly greater than the last accepted version for that key (versions need not be consecutive).
A put stores its value; delete removes a value if present. Deleting a missing key is valid and still advances its version.
A later put must exceed that recorded deletion version. Different keys have independent version sequences.
All invalid streams raise ValueError, never mutate input, and never return partial results.
Output nested values must be independent of inputs and of each other even if input events shared value objects.
Empty list returns both empty dicts. No I/O or persistence is needed.
Only edit events/validation.py, events/replay.py. Run the documented public test command after the final edits.

prompt:
Repair a small configuration command parser. This is a defined grammar, not a shell executor.
lexing.split_words(text) requires a string and returns a list of words. Outside quotes, ASCII space/tab/CR/LF delimit words.
Single or double quotes begin/end quoted fragments, and quote delimiters are removed. Adjacent fragments concatenate
into one word. Whitespace inside quotes is literal. Empty quoted words must be retained; empty/only-delimiter text gives [].
Backslash escapes exactly the next character outside quotes and inside double quotes; inside single quotes it is literal.
A quote of the other kind is literal inside quotes. Unterminated quotes or a dangling escape raise ValueError.
Unicode whitespace other than the four ASCII delimiters is an ordinary character. No comments, expansion, or other shell syntax.
options.parse_assignments(text) uses split_words; every word must be KEY=VALUE, split on the FIRST '='.
KEY must match ASCII [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* exactly. VALUE may be empty or contain more equals signs.
Return a dict. Last duplicate key wins, retaining the key's first insertion order. Validate every word; invalid input raises
ValueError, including non-string text, tokens without '=', empty keys, and invalid keys. Do not execute anything or read environment.
Only edit arguments/lexing.py, arguments/options.py. Run the documented public test command after the final edits.
